historical_claims.anchor: In her study of early printed drama, one of the examples comes from a 1588 English translation of the Roman playwright Terence's Andria.
At points where the dialogue breaks, the printed text uses little sequences of dashes or hyphens, not the tidy three dots we would recognize today.
Jane Austen used dashes and runs of dots in some of her early manuscript writing.
By the nineteenth century, printed punctuation was becoming more standardized, although writers did not stop experimenting.
The first Chicago Manual of Style, published in 1906, specified four spaced periods in many cases where material was omitted from a quotation.
In linguistics, an ellipsis can occur without three dots—or any dots at all.
The linguist Gretchen McCulloch has described a generational difference in how some people use the dots.
McCulloch has emphasized that the difference is connected to how messages are divided.
Signal, for example, describes typing indicators as optional animated dots.
You can type three ordinary periods. Or you can use a single character whose Unicode name is horizontal ellipsis.
In Japanese typography, an ellipsis may be centered vertically rather than resting near the baseline like a period.
In Python, three consecutive periods are a literal value called Ellipsis.
In the array library NumPy, an ellipsis in an index can stand for all the intervening dimensions.
